B-9, as amended (including Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register requirements and applicable regulations); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC related regulations/guidance; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Alberta ISC register and corporate records are filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry and are accessible to the Registrar, law enforcement, tax authorities and financial intelligence units on demand; not a fully public UBO register; FINTRAC and authorized agencies obtain access through statutory gateways)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Secretary of State or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (certification by the competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin); consular legalization only if origin state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public (or equivalent) in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Canadian consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate resolution and power of attorney appointing the Alberta incorporator / registered office agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors and officers against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act) and provincial/domestic watchlists; PEP identification and enhanced due diligence required for foreign PEPs (and domestic PEPs under updated PCMLTFA/legislative amendments), including source-of-funds verification for the ULC share subscription; screening records must be retained for at least 5 years post-relationship per PCMLTFA recordkeeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES electronic filing and authorized service providers) / NUANS Name Search Report (Canadian name pre-screening system for federal-Alberta corporate names)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the Latin (English/French) alphabet; statutory name structure requires distinctive element + descriptive element + legal element ('ULC', 'U.L.C.' or 'Unlimited Liability Company' for an Alberta unlimited liability company); NUANS pre-search must cover identical, confusingly similar and phonetically equivalent names; accents and punctuation are accepted but disregarded in the comparison; non-Roman script names require transliteration into English/French; abbreviations such as '&' are interchangeable with 'and' and grammatical variations do not cure confusion.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Alberta (as a dominant token implying provincial patronage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a 'no-name'/rejection notice from the Nunavut NUANS screening, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Alberta Registrar of Corporations (through the Corporate Registry service channel) within 30 days of the rejection, setting out distinctiveness arguments, evidence of prior use or registration, and letters of no objection from holders of conflicting names; if the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may either file a new NUANS search with a revised name (fresh 90-day reservation) or seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible: Alberta law requires a registered office and records address at a physical, serviceable street address in Alberta (no post office box); a virtual office / registered-agent service address is acceptable for incorporation and statutory compliance. However, for payment processor and bank KYC onboarding (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) and for demonstrating commercial substance to the CRA and Alberta registry, a documented physical operating location, even a small fulfillment/warehouse or home-office address in Alberta, is strongly recommended for lower-risk profile; pure virtual-office-only substance may trigger enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 10-15%) for a non-regulated online retail e-commerce business under ISIC 4791; no routine unannounced physical inspection is statutorily authorized for this sector, but the Alberta Corporate Registry may conduct compliance examinations of registered office records, and the CRA may audit books/records at a designated business address; inspection/EDD review likelihood rises to approximately 25-30% upon first bank account and payment processor onboarding.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; ss. 6–13 (incorporation), ss. 15.1–15.4 (unlimited liability corporations), ss. 19–24 (registered office and records), ss. 101–125 (directors), and s. 211 (annual return)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Form 1), together with Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA for an unlimited liability corporation. No escrow, hold-back, or capital deposit is required. Contributors may subscribe for nominal stated capital, provided the issued share consideration is credited as paid-up capital in the corporate records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: APPROVED at the first meeting of directors of Solar Portable Power Retail ULC: 1. Share Subscription. The founding shareholder's subscription is accepted, and the paid-up capital contribution is recorded. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is fixed at [address in Calgary, Alberta], and the corporate records will be kept there. 3. Directors. [Director Names] are appointed directors to serve until the next annual meeting. 4. Officers. [President], [Treasurer], and [Secretary] are appointed officers. 5. Banking. Management is authorized to open corporate bank accounts and issue share certificates. 6. Governance. The initial by-laws and corporate minute book are approved. DULY RESOLVED on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online portal (CORES) or an authorized Alberta corporate registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request through the Alberta Corporate Registry or an authorized agent. The search must identify no conflicting corporate, trade, or trademark names in Alberta. If available, reserve the selected ULC name for up to 90 days before filing the Articles.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Search Request / Authorization for Registry Agent
Proposed legal name and up to two alternative names
Statement of business purpose (online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflict or query is raised, apply for a new name search with an amended proposed name. A Registry deficiency notice may be cured by filing the corrected search results before the reservation period expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of ULC Articles of Incorporation and Internal Governance Provisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation on Alberta Form 1. Designate the entity as an unlimited liability corporation, authorize the share classes and any special rights and restrictions, and list the first directors and registered office. The articles must be executed by each incorporator or the authorized agent and comply with ABCA Part 2 and section 15.1.
required_dossiers: Name Search Report and reservation certificate
Consent to Act as Director for each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns the draft for correction, revise the deficient provisions and resubmit. A rejection based on statutory non-compliance will not forfeit the reservation if corrected within the deficiency notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles together with the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors through CORES, in person at an Alberta registry office, or by authorized agent. Pay the prescribed filing fee. The Registrar will review the filing for formal compliance and, upon approval, issue a Certificate of Incorporation with the Alberta corporation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, submit the requested corrections and fee within the stated period; a fully corrected package will proceed without loss of the incorporation date. If the application is refused, the agent may request administrative review by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Minutes, By-laws, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office; Alberta Corporate Registry for any subsequent director changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, hold the first board meeting and pass the pro-forma first board resolution. Adopt Bylaw No. 1, approve the share subscription and issuance of share certificates, appoint officers, open the corporate minute book, and record the registered office and records location in the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and government notices
Share subscription agreements and paid-up capital records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director declines appointment, the board may appoint a replacement by written resolution and file an amended Notice of Directors with the Corporate Registry. Missing records are remedied by restating resolutions and dating them as of the original board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax and Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA for a Business Number (BN), GST/HST, payroll (if applicable), and import/export account. Confirm Alberta corporate tax registration and the ULC pass-through elections with the Canada Revenue Agency and Alberta Finance where relevant. Obtain municipal business licence from the local municipality if physical premises will be used.
required_dossiers: ULC articles and entity structure information
Projected revenue and bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Alberta authority queries the registration, amend the online application with the correct entity information and respond to the compliance check letter. Registration can be reactivated or adjusted by written notice to the relevant authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Annual Reporting Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is effective and accessible during normal business hours, and file any update to directors, officers, or registered office promptly. After incorporation, calendar the annual return filing obligation with the Alberta Corporate Registry and maintain the corporate minute book at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return or update notice is queried, file a corrected return through CORES and pay any late fee. Persistent non-compliance may be cured by filing a status restoration application and obtaining an updated certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No separate Alberta industrial licensing board applies to online retail; municipal licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence) and Alberta fire and occupational safety authorities govern physical premises operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels; local municipal business licence and occupancy/fire clearances apply if a warehouse or office is occupied

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (Environmental Assessment and Regulatory Assurance Division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not triggered - Exempt / Registration-level only. E-commerce retail warehousing and distribution do not meet mandatory EIA thresholds under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) and the Activities Designation Regulation. A registration or EIA screening would be required only if the operation later includes battery recycling or high-hazard waste processing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharge is expected. The operation must comply with municipal stormwater and sanitary sewer bylaws, EPEA release-reporting obligations for any accidental discharge, Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives if backup generators are used, and the Alberta Hazardous Waste Regulation for damaged lithium batteries or defective solar panels. Shipment of rejected lithium batteries must additionally comply with Transport Canada's TDG Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense clearance is required. For physical premises, obtain a fire safety approval/occupancy permit from the local fire authority under the Alberta Fire Code, confirm structural loading capacity for racked battery and solar panel storage, and comply with the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code for workplace ergonomics, electrical safety, emergency exits, and lithium-battery handling controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA / Agence du revenu du Canada), federal administrator of the Excise Tax Act (GST/HST) and Income Tax Act; CRA portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-individuals/account-individuals.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO). Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under the Canada-Alberta Tax Collection Agreement. Provincial corporate registry: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Alberta ULC: (i) incorporate under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) through Service Alberta Corporate Registry to obtain the Alberta corporation number; (ii) register with CRA using BRO or Form RC1 and elect Program Accounts RP (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RC (payroll, if applicable); (iii) CRA issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with two-letter program identifiers (e.g., 123456789 RP0001 / RT0001); (iv) for a foreign entity branch that is not separately incorporated in Canada, the branch must obtain a BN, register for GST/HST under the small supplier rules if Canadian taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and obtain an RM (import/export) program account plus a CBSA customs client identifier; (v) GST/HST registration effective from the date the threshold is exceeded or as mutually agreed with CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — An Alberta ULC is a separate legal person subject to Canadian entity-level income tax (federal 38% Part I rate less 13% abatement, yielding a 15% general federal effective rate, plus Alberta 8% general corporate rate; combined approximately 23% before the small business deduction). For U.S. federal tax purposes, the ULC is an eligible entity under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 because its members have unlimited liability; the default classification is disregarded (single member) or partnership (multi-member), permitting pass-through treatment and access to the Canada-U.S. Treaty fiscally transparent entity rule. Territorial scope: worldwide income with foreign tax credits; no tax-exempt zone applies. Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so the 5% GST is the only indirect tax on local supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: U.S. check-the-box election: IRS Form 8832 (due within 75 days of formation) may override the default partnership/disregarded status and elect corporate classification; there is no Canadian federal counterpart election to reclassify a corporation as transparent. Available material elections: GST/HST joint election under ETA s.273 for closely related entities; ETA s.211.1 election for foreign supplier reporting; ITA s.216(1) election on deemed Canadian rental income; ITA s.216.1 election for Canadian resource property income; ITA s.115.1 election to file for treaty-protected Canadian real property gains; ITA s.85 rollover election for property transfers into the ULC; amalgamation election under ITA s.87; and ETA nil-consideration election for inter-corporate supplies. Hybrid mismatch scrutiny applies to ULC pass-through elections under the MLI, GILTI/CFC rules, and ITA s.247 transfer pricing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada); Alberta provincial rate is 0% (no PST / HST), so the effective rate in CA-AB is 5% GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold: mandatory registration when worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. No separate Alberta sales tax registration is required because Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax. Non-resident online sellers may use CRA simplified GST/HST registration (GST494).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime. The CRA operates a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-Invoicing Service (Peppol BIS 3.0 interoperability pilot, 2023 onward). Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns applies to registrants with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million; electronic NETFILE/GST/HST remittance is standard for all registrants. Export declarations must be filed electronically via the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) where the value of exported goods is CAD 2,000 or more, with Form B13A used only in fallback. GST/HST tax invoices must display the supplier BN, date, parties, description, tax amount and rate, and records must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under ETA Schedule VI, Part V: (i) goods (portable battery generators, HS 8504.40 / 8507; solar panels, HS 8541.43) sold to a non-resident buyer are zero-rated if ownership transfers to the buyer and the goods are exported from Canada within 60 days of transfer of ownership (supplier-export) or within 60 days of delivery to the recipient (recipient-export), in accordance with the Export and Exclusion of Property Regulations SOR/88-252; (ii) ancillary services to exported goods (e.g., remote monitoring software, warranties) supplied to a non-resident, non-registrant recipient are zero-rated under s.7 of Part V where they do not relate to Canadian real property or goods situated in Canada and are not rendered to an individual present in Canada; (iii) the ULC must retain sufficient evidence of physical export and settlement; no GST is charged on qualifying export sales, and full input tax credits are recoverable on related inputs, including GST paid at importation on inventory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or electronic filing through CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CES)) covering portable power generators and solar panels
Commercial sales invoice and packing list stating HS classification (HS 8504.40 / HS 8507 for battery generators; HS 8541.43 for solar modules), Incoterms and destination
Transport documentation: Master/House Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) or courier shipment records naming the ULC as exporter and the non-resident buyer as consignee
CBSA proof-of-export evidence: carrier certificate, border exit stamp, freight forwarder confirmation, or CBSA Proof of Export report
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, Stripe settlement report, or card acquirer statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds into the ULC's Canadian account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Invalid zero-rating claims trigger CRA reassessment of the supply at 5% GST, daily compound interest at the CRA prescribed rate, and, where false statements or omissions are made knowingly, a gross negligence penalty under ETA s.280 equal to 25% of net tax (50% for a repeat violation), plus criminal liability under ETA s.327 (on summary conviction, up to CAD 50,000 fine and/or 6 months imprisonment; on indictment, up to CAD 500,000 and/or 5 years). The normal four-year GST/HST reassessment period is suspended where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default or fraud, and clawback of related input tax credits and refunds applies. For export receivables outstanding beyond 180 days, CRA may impute interest income under ITA s.80.4 and s.247 for related-party balances and recharacterize overdue amounts as deemed loans or shareholder benefits under ITA s.15(2); unrelated-party bad debts are governed by ETA and ITA bad debt recovery rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2) is the sole monetary and currency-issuing authority; Canada maintains no separate Foreign Exchange Administration. OSFI licenses deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46); FINTRAC enforces cross-border wire monitoring and EFT reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts with no profit-remittance licensing, registration, or prior approval requirement. The former Exchange Control Act lapsed in 1951 and was never re-enacted. Dividend remittances from the Alberta ULC to a non-resident shareholder attract Part XIII withholding (statutory 25%; reduced to 5% under Article X(2) of the Canada-US Tax Convention (1980, as amended) where the beneficial owner is a corporation holding at least 10% of the voting stock, claimed via Form NR301). Interest on intercompany shareholder loans is generally exempt from Canadian withholding under the treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline applies to export proceeds in Canada. The ULC may invoice in USD or CNH, retain foreign-currency deposits indefinitely, and net supplier payments offshore. Only reporting duties attach: FINTRAC EFTR disclosure for any wire of CAD 10,000 or more and CRA Form T1135 (Foreign Income Verification Statement) where specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000 aggregate cost.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank), Calgary
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Multi-Currency CAD/USD) + Capital Escrow Vault
Operational Account + Cross-Border USD Account (BMO Harris integration)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC), Calgary
Scotiabank (The Bank of Nova Scotia), Calgary

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate and complementary only. Wise Payments Canada Inc. (FINTRAC-registered MSB) and Stripe's Canadian payments entity (RPAA-eligible/registered PSP under the Retail Payment Activities Act, in force November 1, 2024) are lawful rails for multi-currency payables, merchant settlement, and sub-CAD 10,000 vendor replenishments. They are not substitutes for a Tier-1 bank: they lack CDIC deposit insurance, commercial LC issuance, and interbank FX credit lines; the Tier-1 bank account must remain the principal liquidity anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permissible in Canada; however, for a non-resident-owned ULC, Tier-1 banks will normally require a live-video compliance interview with the director(s) and each UBO holding >10%, supplemented by Equifax credit-bureau digital identity verification. A physical in-branch appearance is not a statutory mandate. Hybrid onboarding (e-signature plus video KYC) is the prevailing practice for US-resident directors at RBC, BMO, and TD, provided an Alberta registered office or licensed registered agent is verifiable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident (US) UBO control of an Alberta ULC with unlimited liability and check-the-box pass-through election creates attribution and potential nominee ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Certificate of Status (issued within 90 days); certified Articles and Notice of Articles; ULC shareholder register; UBO organization chart identifying all >10% owners; CRA Business Number confirmation; IRS Form 8832 election evidencing US tax flow-through; board resolutions naming authorized signatories; W-8BEN-E and CRS self-certifications for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket e-commerce inflows with Stripe and Affirm BNPL settlements flagged as third-party payment processor concentration risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe Merchant of Record agreement; Affirm/PayBright merchant contract; 12-month settlement histories; chargeback-to-sales ratio below 0.9%; PCI-DSS Level 1 Attestation of Compliance; refund and dispute policy; supplier purchase orders; product classification declarations (NAICS 443142; HS 8504 inverters, 8507 lithium batteries, 8541 solar cells).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection from the US parent for initial ULC capitalization triggers source-of-funds and business-purpose scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; board resolutions authorizing the capital contribution; six months of parent bank statements; pro-forma cash-flow forecast; board-approved treasury policy; completed CDD questionnaire; Form NR301 where treaty withholding relief is later claimed; written explanation of the ULC tax and legal motivation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Portable solar/battery retail raises goods-specific transport-safety and product-liability red flags (UN3480/UN3481 lithium-ion cells).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transport Canada TDG classification certificates and UN38.3 test summaries; UL/cETL safety certifications for the generator line; Commercial General Liability policy certificate (minimum CAD 2M); supplier factory audit reports; recall and complaint-handling procedures; Health Canada CCPSA incident disclosure confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity is wired via SWIFT MT103 to the ULC's CAD operating account at the Tier-1 bank (e.g., RBC Calgary, BIC ROYCCAT2). Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION - SHARE CAPITAL - [Shareholder Name]' with purpose code 'EQUITY CAPITAL'. Wires of CAD 10,000 or more generate automatic FINTRAC EFTR, so the stated purpose must reconcile with the subscription agreement and board minutes held on file. USD-denominated injections may be credited directly to a dedicated USD cross-border sub-account; conversion to CAD for operating expenses is executed at spot under board-approved FX limits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: (i) Direct supplier telegraphic transfers: SWIFT MT103 plus MT202 COV routed via RBC correspondent (JPMorgan New York) to Bank of China/Hong Kong or China Merchants Bank, settled in USD or CNH; (ii) Irrevocable at-sight documentary letters of credit (UCP600) for purchase orders exceeding CAD 100,000, advised through a Chinese advising bank and payable against B/L, commercial invoice, packing list, and product safety certificates; (iii) Open-account payables below CAD 10,000 executed through Wise or Airwallex; (iv) Consumer refunds and BNPL drawdowns settled via Stripe's Canadian payments entity and Affirm/PayBright into the Tier-1 operational account with D+2 liquidity buffers to mitigate settlement timing risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards under a master FX agreement with board-approved notional limits
CAD/USD FX swaps (spot-forward rollovers) for short-tenor working-capital management
CAD/USD cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term intercompany loan hedging
CNH deliverable forwards and CNY non-deliverable forwards covering China supplier currency exposure
Vanilla CAD/USD options (costless collars and protective puts) for margin-preserving downside protection
Excluded instruments: leveraged speculative spot trading, binary options, and exotic structured derivatives without express treasury policy authorization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Corporate Return (annual filing under the Business Corporations Act, Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation; recurring annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 plus cumulative interest; continued non-filing for 12 or more consecutive months permits the Registrar to administratively strike the ULC off the corporate register, causing dissolution and loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act, Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 6 months after the taxation year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end is due June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months (ITA s.162); prescribed CRA interest; repeat-filing penalty of 10% in certain cases; directors may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Corporate Tax Return (AT1 consolidated with federal T2 schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Tax Services / Canada Revenue Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the federal T2 return — within 6 months after taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid Alberta tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; prescribed interest accrues on unpaid balances; persistent delinquency may trigger provincial collection enforcement and loss of provincial compliance clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (Excise Tax Act, Part IX)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers; instalments due quarterly or monthly where mandated by revenue level or CRA direction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 3% of net GST/HST owing (5% for repeat failure within 3 years) plus daily interest on arrears; chronic non-filing may trigger CRA registration suspension and disallowance of input tax credits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) package — financial statements, auditor waiver consent, director ratification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book and statutory registers; available upon demand to Alberta Corporate Registry, CRA, and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter not more than 15 months after the preceding AGM (Alberta BCA s.112)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM is an offence under the Alberta BCA punishable on summary conviction; directors may be personally liable for compliance defaults; continued neglect may support administrative strike-off by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Alberta Business Corporations Act ss.154-155, an auditor is optional where the ULC is non-distributing and all shareholders give unanimous consent; a distributing corporation with gross revenue below CAD 1,000,000 is similarly exempt. Mandatory independent audit applies only to distributing corporations that exceed the threshold or where shareholders fail to waive the auditor appointment; the small private ULC retains full exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) required for public/distributing entities; closely held non-distributing ULCs may apply ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, Part II). Internal tax-basis records are permitted where no financial statements are circulated to shareholders; the ULC pass-through election under Income Tax Regulations s.198.1 does not remove Alberta statutory bookkeeping duties.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta requires every corporation, including a ULC, to maintain a current register of individuals with significant control (ISC) at its registered office. The register must be amended within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control; it is not filed annually with the Alberta registry but must be produced within 10 days on demand by CRA, law enforcement, securities regulators, or the registry. The ULC must therefore reconcile and confirm the ISC register at each AGM and after every share movement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Register of Registered Office (address and agent)
Minute Book containing Articles, By-laws, AGM resolutions and written consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 where statutory audit waiver is in force; USD 2,200 - 5,900 (CAD 3,000 - 8,000) for a voluntary review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate in Alberta = federal Part I rate 15% + Alberta general rate 8%; 11% combined rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) available only if the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation ('CCPC') claiming the small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income — generally unavailable when the ULC is controlled by a U.S. parent.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday for on-line retail in Canada or Alberta. Applicable reliefs: (i) federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development investment tax credit of 15% (non-refundable) on qualifying Canadian R&D (not for pure resale); (ii) clean technology investment tax credits (30% refundable) only for qualifying investments in specified solar-energy-generation equipment used in Canada (not for inventory resale); (iii) capital cost allowance deductions, including Class 8 (20% DB) for computing equipment, Class 50 (55% DB) for computer hardware, Class 12 (100%) for software; (iv) existing non-capital loss carryforwards; (v) the 5% federal GST is collectable and remitted with input tax credits (no Alberta provincial sales tax).
